extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and applicants/attorneys preparing or prosecuting nonprovisional international design applications (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examiner form paragraphs governing prosecution of nonprovisional international design applications: drawing treatment (broken lines/coloring), restriction/election consequences, 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections and responses, foreign priority/benefit claim timing and documentary requirements (37 CFR 1.55, 1.78), and use of WIPO DAS/PDX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renumbering of drawing figures not required after cancellation of non-elected embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Renumbering of the figures following cancellation of non-elected embodiments is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended, to maintain consistency with the published International Registration, that the numbering of drawing figures included in the elected Group not be changed even if non-elected embodiments are cancelled. Any amendment to drawing figures should comply with 37 CFR 1.1026 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions (see Section 405 regarding numbering of reproductions). Examiners should use form paragraph (FP) 29.102 to remind applicants that renumbering is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider correction of inventorship when restriction cancels non-elected designs (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should consider the need to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 as a result of a restriction requirement that cancels non-elected designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction of inventorship after an Office action on the merits is subject to an additional fee under 37 CFR 1.48(c). Examiners should remind applicants (use FP 29.102) about possible inventorship correction and the additional fee. If no practitioner of record, include FP 29.100 Reply Reminder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend application to cancel figures/descriptions for non-elected groups when replying to restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: In replying to a restriction refusal electing a Group for prosecution, applicant should consider amending the application to cancel the drawing figures and remove the description corresponding to the non-elected Group(s), and to correct inventorship, as appropriate, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should note that correcting inventorship after an Office action on the merits will require an additional fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48(c). Examiner Note: add the specified paragraph at the end of a restriction requirement in a nonprovisional international design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of broken/dotted lines or coloring to indicate matter for which protection is not sought (Administrative Instruction 403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Instruction 403 allows matter shown in a reproduction for which protection is not sought to be indicated by broken or dotted lines or coloring (and/or in the description referred to in Rule 7(5)(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using broken/dotted lines or coloring to show matter not sought for protection, applicants are encouraged to include an explanation of the purpose of the broken/dotted lines or coloring in the description to avoid uncertainty as to scope. Applicants are also encouraged not to rely solely on a description to indicate excluded matter but to also identify it in the reproduction via broken/dotted lines or coloring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Undescribed broken lines (Form paragraph 29.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as indefinite where the reproductions include broken lines that are not described in the specification and the scope of the claimed design cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome the rejection by inserting a statement immediately preceding the claim (provided it does not introduce new matter) such as: 'The broken line showing of [structure] is for the purpose of illustrating [portions of the article/environmental structure] and forms no part of the claimed design.' Examiner instructions provide bracketed insertion points for figure numbers, structure name, and whether 'portions of the article' or 'environmental structure.' Use this form paragraph in international design applications with undescribed broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Undescribed broken lines as boundary (Form paragraph 29.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as indefinite where the reproductions include undescribed broken lines serving as a boundary and the scope of the claimed design cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome the rejection by inserting a statement immediately preceding the claim (provided it does not introduce new matter) such as: 'The [type] broken line(s) define the bounds of the claimed design and form no part thereof.' Examiner Note indicates bracketed fields: figure numbers and type of broken line (e.g., dashed, dot-dash). Use when broken lines function as boundary lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Unclear use of coloring (Form paragraph 29.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as indefinite where the reproductions include coloring that is not described in the specification and the scope of the claimed design cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the coloring identifies matter for which protection is not sought, applicant may overcome the rejection by inserting a statement immediately preceding the claim (provided it does not introduce new matter) such as: 'The portion of the design shown in the color [color] is for the purpose of illustrating [portions of the article/environmental structure] and forms no part of the claimed design.' Examiner Note: insert figure numbers and identify the color indicating excluded matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion to overcome rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) by converting undescribed portions to broken lines or coloring (Form paragraph 29.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may indicate that protection is not sought for those portions of the reproductions considered indefinite and nonenabling by amending the reproductions to color those portions or convert them to broken lines, and amending the specification to include a statement that such portions form no part of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not introduce new matter (see 35 U.S.C. 132, 37 CFR 1.121). Use this form paragraph only in an international design application. Insert the title of the article into the bracketed field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) to nonprovisional international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) apply to nonprovisional international design applications (see 35 U.S.C. 389).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice set forth in MPEP § 1504.04 regarding considerations under 35 U.S.C. 112 is generally applicable to nonprovisional international design applications; additional considerations relevant to international design applications are discussed in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority filing time limit (37 CFR 1.55) — 12 months (6 months for design)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application must be filed not later than twelve months after the foreign application's filing date, except in the case of a design application where the period is six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is subject to paragraph (c) (delayed filing restoration) and other exceptions. For international design applications and measurement of the period, see MPEP §§ 2906–2908 and the filing date assigned by the International Bureau. Where delayed, the right of priority may be restored under 37 CFR 1.55(c) and MPEP § 213.03, subsection III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority for delayed filing under 37 CFR 1.55(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subsequent application is filed after the twelve/ six month period but within two months from its expiration, the right of priority may be restored under PCT Rule 26bis.3 for international applications, or upon petition if the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to restore must include: (1) the priority claim in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(6)) identifying the foreign application by number/country/date; (2) the petition fee per § 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information. For petitions filed on or after May 13, 2015, filing location rules apply (filed in subsequent application or earliest nonprovisional claiming benefit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing priority claim in original 35 U.S.C. 111(a) application
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the claim for priority must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application, except as provided in paragraph (e) and with exceptions for design applications and some pre-November 29, 2000 filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The priority claim must be presented in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(6)) identifying the foreign application (application number, country, day, month, year). Time periods do not apply if the later-filed application is a design patent or certain older filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing priority claim for international applications entering national stage (35 U.S.C. 371)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, the claim for priority must be made within the time limit set forth in the PCT and the Regulations under the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PCT deadlines and national stage rules; see paragraph (e) exceptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed priority claim (petition) — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A delayed priority claim not presented within the required time is considered waived unless accepted under the petition provisions; acceptance requires a petition with specific materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to accept a delayed claim must be accompanied by: (1) the priority claim in an ADS identifying the foreign application; (2) a certified copy of the foreign application unless previously submitted or an exception applies; (3) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)); and (4) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may request additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing certified copy of foreign application (37 CFR 1.55(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the foreign application must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the U.S. application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application for 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications (design applications excepted). For 35 U.S.C. 371 national stage entries, the certified copy must be filed within PCT time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed within the specified time and no exception applies, a petition showing good and sufficient cause for the delay plus the petition fee under § 1.17(g) is required. See paragraphs (h)–(j) for situations where the certified copy requirement may be considered satisfied (e.g., copy in another US patent or use of WIPO DAS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that priority claim, certified copy, and translation be filed during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority claim and certified copy of the foreign application must be filed during the pendency of the application, unless filed with an accepted petition; if filed after the issue fee is paid, the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require earlier filing of these documents in certain proceedings (interference/derivation) or when necessary to overcome a reference or as deemed necessary by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation of non-English foreign application — limited requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An English language translation of a non-English foreign application is not generally required, except when: (i) the application is involved in an interference or derivation proceeding, (ii) necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner, or (iii) specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, the translation must be filed together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement may be satisfied by copy in another U.S. patent or application
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for a certified copy of the foreign application (paragraphs (f) and (g)) will be considered satisfied if a U.S. reissue patent or a prior-filed nonprovisional application for which benefit is claimed already contains such a certified copy and is identified as containing the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the relevant U.S. patent or prior-filed application as containing the certified copy when claiming satisfaction under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO DAS / priority document exchange (PDX) can satisfy certified copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a priority claim made under Hague Agreement Rule 7(5)(c) is accompanied by a WIPO Digital Access Service (DAS) access code (Administrative Instruction 408), the USPTO may automatically attempt retrieval of the priority document via WIPO DAS; retrieval will satisfy the certified copy requirement under 37 CFR 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DM/1 form (or IB electronic interface) has a field for the WIPO access code. If the code is not provided initially, it may be added via a corrected application data sheet and request for corrected filing receipt. Applicants bear ultimate responsibility for ensuring the priority document is filed during pendency and before patent issuance; they are encouraged to provide the WIPO access code early and confirm receipt. Note numeric formats required for identifying international design applications for DAS retrieval (WIPONNNNN, WIPONNNNNN, or NNNNNNNNN for indirect/paper filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Copy procedure to satisfy certified copy requirement temporarily
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an 'Interim Copy' of the original foreign application labeled as such, with a separate cover sheet identifying the foreign application, may be used to satisfy the certified copy requirement temporarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interim Copy and cover sheet must be filed within the later of sixteen months from the prior foreign filing date, four months from the actual filing date of a U.S. application under 111(a), four months from national stage commencement under 371(b) or (f), four months from initial PCT submission to enter the national stage, or with an appropriate petition. A certified copy must still be filed within the period specified in paragraph (g)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods are not extendable (subject to listed exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth in this section (37 CFR 1.55) are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are, however, subject to 35 U.S.C. 21(b) (and § 1.7(a)), PCT Rule 80.5, and Hague Agreement Rule 4(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 386(c) — entitlement to benefit of prior national or international design filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States shall be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of a prior national application, prior international application as defined in section 351(c) designating the United States, or a prior international design application designating the United States; similarly, a national application shall be entitled to the benefit of a prior international design application designating the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claim for the benefit of an earlier filing date is based on a prior international application which designated but did not originate in the United States, the Director may require filing of a certified copy of such application together with an English translation if it was filed in another language.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.78 — requirements to claim benefit under 119(e), 120/121/365(c)/386(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming benefit of earlier filing dates: each prior-filed application must name the inventor or joint inventor named in the later application and must be (i) an international application entitled to a filing date under PCT Article 11 and designating the United States; (ii) an international design application entitled to a filing date under § 1.1023 and designating the United States; or (iii) a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) entitled to a filing date per § 1.53(b) or (d) with the basic filing fee paid during pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for a continuing prosecution application filed under § 1.53(d), any later nonprovisional/international application that claims benefit must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each prior-filed application identifying it by application number (series code and serial number), international application number and international filing date, or international registration number and filing date under § 1.1023. See additional provisions in MPEP for continued prosecution/CPA exceptions.
